Application of Soft Skills

Soft skills for nurses — communication, teamwork, empathy, time management and professional behaviour.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • List key soft skills for nursing
  • Describe empathy and active listening
  • Explain teamwork and time management in a ward

In simple words

Soft skills are the personal and social skills that help a nurse work well with patients, families and the team. Technical knowledge matters, but soft skills make the difference between good and great care.

Key soft skills: communication, empathy, teamwork, time management, stress management and professional behaviour.

Key soft skills

Skill What it means
Communication Clear speaking, listening and body language
Empathy Understanding and sharing the patient’s feelings
Active listening Fully focusing on what the patient says
Teamwork Working with doctors, aides and other nurses
Time management Prioritising tasks and using time well
Professional behaviour Punctuality, honesty, boundaries, confidentiality

Empathy vs sympathy

  • Empathy — understand the patient’s feeling (“I can see this is hard for you”).
  • Sympathy — feel sorry for the patient (“I feel sorry for you”).

Empathy builds trust; sympathy can seem pitying.

Teamwork and time management

  • Ward work is a team effort — nurses, doctors, nursing assistants, therapists and cleaners.
  • Handovers pass information between shifts; use SBAR (Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation).
  • Prioritise: urgent and important tasks first (airway, breathing, circulation, safety).

🔴 Empathy builds trust

Empathy = understand the patient’s feeling. Say “I can see this is hard for you” rather than just “I feel sorry for you.”

Where the nurse uses this

  • Handover — use SBAR to pass clear, complete information.
  • Patient talk — listen without interrupting; reflect feelings.
  • Team conflict — speak respectfully, focus on the patient, involve the charge nurse if needed.
  • Prioritise — do urgent tasks first; delegate appropriately.
  • Boundaries — be friendly but professional; do not share personal details.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Soft skills: communication, empathy, active listening, teamwork, time management, professional behaviour.
  2. Empathy understands the patient’s feeling; sympathy feels sorry for them.
  3. Active listening means fully focusing on the speaker.
  4. SBAR structures handover: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
  5. Prioritise urgent and important tasks first.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Professional behaviour includes punctuality, honesty, boundaries and confidentiality.
  2. Teamwork includes doctors, nurses, aides and therapists.
  3. Time management reduces stress and missed care.
  4. Good communication improves patient satisfaction and safety.

📌 Memory trick

Handover: SBAR — Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

60-second revision

  • Soft skills = personal and social skills for working with people.
  • Communication, empathy, listening, teamwork, time management, professionalism.
  • Empathy = understand; sympathy = feel sorry.
  • SBAR handover: Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.
  • Prioritise urgent and important tasks first.

Test yourself

Empathy means:

Answer: B. Empathy is understanding and sharing the patient's feelings; sympathy is feeling sorry.

SBAR in handover stands for:

Answer: A. SBAR = Situation, Background, Assessment, Recommendation.

Active listening means:

Answer: B. Active listening is giving full attention to the speaker without interrupting.

Which is a soft skill?

Answer: B. Communication is a soft skill; the others are technical clinical skills.

Urgent and important tasks should be done:

Answer: C. Time management means doing urgent and important tasks first.
